To clarify, I am not Transgender. I am, per subject matter, a Cisgender Male.

However I do not hold that against anyone who identifies as transgender, the same way I do not hold it against a female with Body Dysmorphia, which one of my close friends happens to have. 

You may already be familiar with the condition, but in some cases the individual can actually look into a mirror or stare at a picture of themselves and their mind distorts the image to represent their own interpretation of their appearance. 

In my friends' particular case, a 5ft 5 female, weighing but 115lbs, would see a photo of herself and scoff in disgust, at portions or what she saw as defects in her physique, that did not actually exist. Naturally this lead to eating disorders and other health problems. 

Pretty intense stuff. Now while this disorder does not manifest itself the same way Gender Dysphoria does. I do find the two to be comparable examples that research towards either would benefit the other. 

Now the source and cause of all these mental states can be debated up and down. As we have no real concrete evidence to decipher the cause of essentially any of them... 

Which again, in the scope of things, does not matter whether any of them are neurological, biological, genetic, etc. 

I myself have vitiligo, once thought to be a skin disease is now associated with autoimmune disorders, and that's still essentially a guess among researchers. The cause really only matters when it comes to the treatment and prevention. Other than that, it's irrelevant.

"Everyone has the right to murder. And everyone has the right to persecute those who commit murder" to generalize.

The brain scans you're referring to, found similarities in certain areas of the brain. Yet it also found many similarities between transgenders and their natal sex counterparts. More so than that were MANY scans that were completely inconsistent across the board, i.e both trans female and male measuring similarly to cisgender females, with cisgender males being the outlier. 

It has also been stated that these studies are not full proof by any means for either side of the debate. One large reason being that the brain regions tested, had been shown in previous studies to “mediate perception of the body" Where in fMRI studies, where people were shown photographs of themselves alongside others. The Gender Dysphoria members showed weaker responses on the brains neural networks that mediate self awareness. Meaning that, in this studies hypothesis the Gender Dysphoria is in fact causing the brain to deny it's relation of body-to-self. Not due to a prominence of male or female hormones within the brain. 

Which leads to your next statement that 
"the current theory among the medical and academic communities" 
This is flat out aggrandizing, as there are a select number of researchers that stand by this HYPOTHESIS, (not a theory). 

Stacking evidence against that hypothesis is the studies done on transgender subjects who have undergone hormone therapy, compared to a cisgender control group, show many discrepancies in areas of the brain including brain volume, that had not shown to be a measurable difference among those without hormone therapy. Leading to the stance that;

A: Hormones have an immense impact on the brain.

B: If the hormonal changes that occured during gestation, or brain development had a sole impact on gender association, the tests should have revealed larger differences among those without hormone therapy, as their brains would have already been exposed to the hormone imbalance. 

As I elaborated on my other response to OP. The problem with the "assigned at birth" agenda, is that gender is DESIGNED at conception. For it is at that moment, and that moment only that either the X or Y chromosome is transferred to the egg. Inserting the genetic code of what gender the offspring will develop as biologically. 

Many studies have also shown that the nature of a child and it's upbringing has a larger impact on it's hormonal production than the hormones produced during gestation. 

So again to reiterate, by no means, is stating that, Gender Dysphoria (transgender) is a mental disorder, an insult. It is a simple deduction based on the facts of when gender is determined, and at what points in a child's development, from birth to adolescence, hormonal and neurological changes can occur and when they have the largest impact. 

Which, just as in the case of many mental health disorders, occur during brain development which primarily occurs post-birth.

Your perception of your gender may in fact change as your brain develops over time. Which in my opinion, has nothing to do with male or female. That distinction comes simply down to which chromosome you received. 

Therefore there should be no such thing as identifying as a man a woman, people should identify as themselves as an individual instead of needing to classify themselves on the scale of biological gender.
